topic: Risk assessment documentation in mental health

audits.title: Assessing the quality of risk assessment conducted for new psychiatry inpatients
audits.standard: Junior doctors document risk assessment in admission clerking
audits.setting: Two acute psychiatric wards, East Lancashire Hospitals NHS Trust

cycle1.result: 12/30 (40%) had a junior doctor risk assessment in clerking; 14 (47%) had none on admission.

audits.intervention: Teaching on risk assessment and a risk assessment template.
audits.other_findings: Of 12 assessments, only 1 mentioned absconding and 8 vulnerability; re-audit under way.
audits.citation: Handa N. Assessing the quality of risk assessment conducted for new psychiatry inpatients. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S80-S80.

audits.title: Risk Assessments of Patients Admitted to Mixed Inpatient Psychiatric Wards: A Clinical Audit
audits.standard: Acute care group standard: patients with known risk to the opposite sex not admitted to mixed sex wards; comprehensive risk assessment on admission and escalation of risks to MDT
audits.setting: Mixed sex inpatient psychiatric wards, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust

cycle1.result: Full risk assessment documented in 50%; historical risks 40%; admission clerking contained risk assessment in 70% and risks to others in 60%; 30% had risks to the opposite sex but none were escalated to the MDT

audits.intervention: Recommended: specific guidance for documenting risk assessments and teaching for healthcare professionals
audits.other_findings: Prompted by a serious incident on a mixed sex ward. Re-audit scheduled for March 2022.
audits.citation: Bennett S, Delaffon V. Risk Assessments of Patients Admitted to Mixed Inpatient Psychiatric Wards: A Clinical Audit. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S150-S151.

audits.title: Inpatient Ward Review Safety Documentation Re-audit
audits.standard: Psychiatry Ward Review Safety Checklist (6 items: legal status, resuscitation, capacity, deterioration, physical health, medication review); target 80% completion
audits.setting: Tower Ward, Landermere Centre, Clacton On Sea; inpatient psychiatric ward (Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust)

cycle1.result: 2019 audit: legal status 93%, resuscitation status 39%, capacity 14%, deteriorating health 64%, physical health 69%, medication review 81%

audits.intervention: Ward Review Safety Checklist on the Trust electronic clinical recording system (created 2018)

cycle2.result: Legal status 88% week 1, 100% mid-stay and pre-discharge; resuscitation 42%, 53%, 45%; capacity 92%, 92%, 67%; deteriorating health 100% at all reviews; physical health 92%, 92%, 88%; medication review 88%, 83%, 75%

audits.other_findings: Compliance was above 80% for all items except resuscitation status, which stayed at 40–50% across all reviewed weeks.
audits.citation: Zinchenko O, Meakin Y, Davies L, Bhan - Kotwal S. Inpatient Ward Review Safety Documentation Re-audit. BJPsych Open. 2022;8(Suppl 1):S181-S181.

audits.title: Documentation Gaps in Suicide Risk Assessments: A Resident-Level Clinical Audit Using the C-SSRS Standard
audits.standard: C-SSRS: documentation of ideation, behaviour and use of a structured tool 100%; risk level and safety planning 90%
audits.setting: Department of psychiatry, Faisalabad Medical University (residents' records)

cycle1.result: Suicidal ideation documented 79.7%; behaviour 47.5%; intensity or frequency 25.4%; C-SSRS used 0.8%; risk level 2.5%; protective factors 0.8%; safety plan 0.8%.

audits.other_findings: Poor documentation was consistent across all residency levels. Recommended resident training and building C-SSRS into electronic records.
audits.citation: ALI I, Dogar I, Mustafa H, Asgher A, Zahra F. Documentation Gaps in Suicide Risk Assessments: A Resident-Level Clinical Audit Using the C-SSRS Standard. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S272-S273. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11569.

audits.title: Audit of Completion of Risk Assessment on Admission & Discharge - Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore
audits.standard: Risk assessment within 24 hours of admission covering all risk domains, risk management plan, and review and update before discharge
audits.setting: Psychiatry inpatient unit, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Admission risk assessment within 24 hours 64%; documentation in notes 84%; risk from others 68%; risk management plan 72%; review before discharge 40%; update before discharge 40%.

audits.intervention: Staff education, risk-assessment checklists displayed on the ward, and ward-round reminders.

cycle2.result: Admission risk assessment within 24 hours 92%; documentation 96%; risk from others 88%; risk management plan 88%; review before discharge 84%; update before discharge 80%.

audits.other_findings: Audit ran over two months. Standardised admission and discharge proformas are recommended.
audits.citation: Siraj S, Ijaz M, Ali M, Jannat S, Siraj S. Audit of Completion of Risk Assessment on Admission & Discharge - Department of Psychiatry, Gulab Devi Teaching Hospital, Lahore. BJPsych Open. 2026;12(S1):S344-S345. doi:10.1192/bjo.2026.11840.

audits.title: Improving risk assessments for CAMHS admissions at Great Ormond Street Hospital
audits.standard: Ward risk assessment policy: risk assessment within one working day of admission
audits.setting: Mildred Creek Unit, inpatient CAMHS ward, Great Ormond Street Hospital

cycle1.result: Average delay between admission and risk assessment was 2 weeks.

audits.intervention: Posters prompting on-call liaison doctors, written and verbal information for new junior doctors, and a risk prompt added to the weekly ward round proforma.

cycle2.result: No patients had risk assessment delayed beyond the next working day.

audits.citation: Stock L, Evans S. Improving risk assessments for CAMHS admissions at Great Ormond Street Hospital. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S107-S107.

audits.title: Analysis of Suicides Reported as Adverse Events in Psychiatry Resulted in Nine Quality Improvement Initiatives.
audits.standard: Audit chart developed by expert panel for suicide risk assessment and clinical care
audits.setting: Psychiatry services, North Denmark Region (Aalborg University Hospital Psychiatry)

cycle1.result: Suicide risk assessments adequately documented in 6 of 35 cases; relatives involved in 4 of 35 risk assessments.

audits.other_findings: Risk assessments emphasised suicidal ideation over known risk factors; panel proposed nine quality improvement areas (training, documentation, involving relatives, communication, data sharing).
audits.citation: Mackenhauer J, Winsløv JH, Holmskov J, Brødsgaard I, Larsen TG, Mainz J. Analysis of Suicides Reported as Adverse Events in Psychiatry Resulted in Nine Quality Improvement Initiatives. Crisis. 2022;43(4):307-314. doi:10.1027/0227-5910/a000787. PMID: 34003020.

audits.title: Evaluation of Suicide Risk Assessment Documentation Standards in Psychiatric Outpatient Clinics
audits.standard: NICE NG225 and local trust standards for suicide risk assessment documentation
audits.setting: Psychiatric outpatient clinics, Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Consent and confidentiality 4%; history of self-harm 28%; protective factors 52%; risk formulation 62%; plan and intent in those with suicidal ideation 0%; access to means 6%; shared decision-making 98%

audits.intervention: Audit findings summarised and fed back to clinicians

cycle2.result: Consent and confidentiality 76%; history of self-harm 76%; protective factors 78%; risk formulation 82%; plan and intent 84%; access to means 14%; shared decision-making 84%

audits.other_findings: Exploration of access to means stayed low and shared decision-making documentation fell. Suicidal ideation was present in 28% at baseline and 50% at re-audit.
audits.citation: Honarvar E, Ashraf F, Pathak A, Pathak A. Evaluation of Suicide Risk Assessment Documentation Standards in Psychiatric Outpatient Clinics. BJPsych Open. ;12(Suppl 1):S301-S301.
